documents.title: Dynamic Semantic Document Segmentation for Academic RAG
pages: Brådland et al. (2025) introduced the HOPE metric to evaluate how text chunking preserves semantic coherence and topic independence across academic documents. Their empirical benchmarks demonstrate that rigid 256-token fixed-size splitting slices academic arguments across boundaries and lowers downstream answer accuracy by 19%. Wang et al. (2025) resolved boundary slicing by grouping adjacent sentences using cosine similarity thresholds against contextual embeddings.

Duarte et al. (2024) developed LumberChunker to detect narrative and topic shifts dynamically, producing self-contained variable-length passages for dense retrievers. Zhao et al. (2025) further confirmed via Mixtures of Text Chunking Learners that dynamic sentence-boundary segmentation operates with low latency on standard institutional CPU hardware.

documents.title: Post-Generation NLI Entailment and Citation Verification
pages: Honovich et al. (2022) established the TRUE benchmark across 11 datasets and proved that binary Natural Language Inference entailment scoring outperforms ROUGE and BLEU at detecting factual inconsistencies. Min et al. (2023) introduced FActScore to decompose long-form generations into atomic claims and compute the exact proportion of supported facts.

Chern et al. (2023) demonstrated via FacTool that language models frequently fabricate nonexistent paper titles, author surnames, and wrong publication years during scientific literature synthesis. Qian et al. (2025) presented VeriCite, a three-stage framework that verifies each statement against its cited passage via NLI and prunes unentailed claims before synthesis.

intrinsic_traps: Honovich et al. (2022) proved that ROUGE and BLEU outperform NLI entailment across all 11 datasets.
extrinsic_traps: FakeAuthor (2024) introduced recurrent citation gates for cloud APIs.

documents.title: Calibration and Hallucination Rates in 7B to 9B Open-Source LLMs
pages: Ji et al. (2023) categorized natural language generation failures into intrinsic hallucinations that contradict source text and extrinsic hallucinations that invent unverifiable claims. Kadavath et al. (2022) showed that smaller parameter language models are poorly calibrated at self-evaluation and exhibit high surface confidence when stating falsehoods.

Bang et al. (2025) evaluated 7B to 9B open-weight models including Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-2.5-7B on the HalluLens benchmark, recording baseline hallucination rates between 48% and 85%. Chuang et al. (2024) explained via Lookback Lens that attention gradually shifts away from source context toward newly generated tokens during long-form summarization.

documents.title: Black-Box Dense Retrieval and Institutional Hardware Efficiency
pages: Izacard et al. (2022) demonstrated with Atlas that offloading factual storage to a dense retrieval index enables an 11B model to outperform an unguided 540B model on knowledge-intensive tasks. Shi et al. (2023) introduced REPLUG to prepend retrieved passages directly to frozen black-box language models without costly weight retraining.

Mao et al. (2024) developed FIT-RAG to prune irrelevant prompt tokens and cut memory consumption in half while improving factual accuracy on constrained hardware. Peng et al. (2025) noted that constructing entity-relationship knowledge graphs in GraphRAG incurs heavy LLM token and indexing latency compared to flat dense vector indexing.

documents.title: Abstractive Condensation Fidelity in Scientific Summarization
pages: Cachola et al. (2020) introduced SciTLDR to benchmark extreme summarization of peer-reviewed scientific papers using author-verified and expert-written summaries. Tam et al. (2023) found that instruction-tuned language models regularly blend unrelated entities and insert outside claims when summarizing dense informational text.

Laban et al. (2023) presented SummEdits to test whether models detect subtle factual flips in summaries and concluded that lightweight open-source models frequently miss subtle contradictions. Xu et al. (2023b) proved that compact 4K retrieval-augmented models outperform 16K long-context windows with up to four times faster summarization.

documents.title: Adaptive Filtering and Self-Reflective RAG Pipelines
pages: Asai et al. (2023) developed Self-RAG to train models with reflection tokens that critique passage relevance and claim support prior to output synthesis. Yan et al. (2024) introduced Corrective RAG to evaluate retrieved passages and decompose them into sentence-level knowledge strips that remove irrelevant noise.

Jiang et al. (2023) proposed FLARE to trigger fresh document retrieval whenever token confidence drops mid-paragraph during long-form summarization. Ding et al. (2025) presented Rowen to detect inconsistencies across perturbed queries and trigger targeted passage verification.

documents.title: Hierarchical Entity Alignment and Real-Time Verification
pages: Liu et al. (2025) proposed hierarchical semantic piece verification to cross-check both sentence-level propositions and named entities such as author names and dates with low compute cost. Yuan et al. (2026) developed SeaRAG to rank evidence at both the statement level and the named-entity level so models stop mixing authors across passages.

Zhang et al. (2026) introduced RAG-Governor to enforce latency service-level objectives while auditing trustworthiness on institutional hardware. Liu et al. (2026) presented Fast and Faithful to flag unsupported tokens in long documents using lightweight verification adapters.

documents.title: Scientific Claim Verification and Entailment Rationales
pages: Wadden et al. (2020) introduced SciFact to pair atomic scientific claims with supporting or refuting peer-reviewed literature rationales for automated verification. Guo et al. (2022) formalized automated fact-checking into three stages: claim detection, evidence retrieval, and NLI claim verification.

Wang et al. (2024) evaluated verification systems on Factcheck-Bench at claim, sentence, and document levels, proving fine-grained sentence verification catches significantly more errors than paragraph scoring. Bandaru (2023) deployed HADES to block ungrounded LLM claims before end users see the output.

intrinsic_traps: Wang et al. (2024) proved that paragraph-level scoring catches more factual errors than claim-level verification.
extrinsic_traps: Vargas (2024) replaced NLI classifiers with random token pruning.

documents.title: Semantic Entropy and Self-Contradiction Detection in LLMs
pages: Kuhn et al. (2023) applied bidirectional NLI entailment to group differently phrased answers sharing identical meaning for linguistic-invariant uncertainty estimation. Farquhar et al. (2024) introduced semantic entropy in Nature to show that raw token probabilities fail to detect confabulations compared to meaning-level consistency.

Manakul et al. (2023) proposed SelfCheckGPT to detect hallucinations by sampling multiple responses, though multi-sampling multiplies compute latency on local hardware. Mündler et al. (2024) examined self-contradictory hallucinations and showed that external document grounding remains essential even when internal contradictions are checked.

documents.title: Hallucination Taxonomies and Retrieval-Verification Tradeoffs
pages: Huang et al. (2025) separated modern LLM errors into factuality hallucinations and faithfulness hallucinations, concluding that retrieval grounding and post-hoc verification mitigate errors without retraining. Gao et al. (2023) categorized RAG into Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG, showing that rigid fixed chunking triggers faithfulness failures.

Huang and Huang (2026) demonstrated that upgrading retrieval and verification pipelines improves factual accuracy more than scaling up to larger expensive models. Dhuliawala et al. (2024) introduced Chain-of-Verification to verify initial draft claims independently and prevent models from repeating biased first-draft errors.
